- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% in subsequent periods.  
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤ 0.33) or shows negative momentum, model frequently underestimates; adjust upward by 1–4% to account for mean reversion.  
- Model consistently overpredicts in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is volatile; apply lag correction by reducing forecast by 0.5–2% for short-term horizons.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 1–3% downward adjustment to align with historical volatility patterns.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate when sentiment is high and underestimate when sentiment is low; apply sentiment-weighted smoothing: +1% if sentiment > 0.67, -1% if sentiment < 0.33.
